full_judgment:
2. The material facts are that the plaintiff-respondent was married to the defendant-petitioner and thereafter they were divorced. Subsequent thereto, the plaintiff filed a suit for realisation of dower money and maintenance. The suit was ultimately decreed and the plaintiff put the decree into the execution. On the prayer of the defendant-judgment-debtor 40 instalments were granted by the Court, each instalment being Tk. 13,875.02 only to be paid by the month. The first instalment was due to be paid from July, 1998. The first instalment was not paid by the defendant. Consequently the plaintiff filed an application for executing the first instalment and sending the petitioner to suffer imprisonment for three months. The petitioner suffered imprisonment but did not pay the amount of the first instalment. The petitioner did not also pay any instalment which was subsequently due. Then again the petitioner put the decree into execution for further imprisonment for three months for the failure to pay the instalment of the month of August, 1998. This amount was not also paid by the defendant. Thus, the main question arose in the execution proceeding whether the subsequent execution against the petitioner is maintainable or not. 

 4. From the materials on record it is found that on the own seeking of the petitioner 40 instalment's were granted but the petitioner did not pay a single instalment. Hence, the execution was started for one instalment only in respect of Tk. 13,000/- and odd whereas the total decree was for Tk. three lac and odd and as such the entire decretal amount remained unpaid. As a matter of fact, the execution was for one instalment and there is no legal bar to proceeding with the executing under section 16(3) of the Family Court Ordinance for the unpaid amount. The entire amount having remained unpaid, there is no legal bar to proceeding with the subsequent execution.
